_comment: EdgeCDSS — vital sign ranges and conflict cautions.
CLINICAL CONTENT. This file is config so the thresholds and the drug lists
can be reviewed and edited by a clinician without touching Python. vitals.py
reads it at import; if it is missing or unparseable the built-in defaults in
vitals.py are used and the reason is printed.
ranges[]  plausible physiological bounds. A LABELLED vital outside these is
rejected with a visible note rather than stored — 'BP 400/300' is
a typo, and silently believing it is worse than not reading it.
These are plausibility bounds, NOT normal ranges: 'hr' spans 10-300
because a real patient can present anywhere in there.
cautions[]  when.<vital> gives the comparison that arms the rule, and drugs[]
the agents it applies to. A caution is NOT a block: it appends a
visible line and downgrades a SAFE verdict to NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW.
It never blocks a response and never releases one.
group     optional. Rules sharing a group are ONE caution with
more than one way to arm it, and at most one of them speaks —
the first armed rule in table order. Hypotension uses it: SBP
below 90 and MAP below 65 are the same warning about the same
patient, and a pressure like 82/40 arms both. Two sentences
differing only in which number they quote is how a caution stops
being read.
Deliberately narrow. A caution that fires on most responses stops
being read, which is worse than not having it.
NOTE: ketamine is deliberately absent from the hypotension and
respiratory lists. It is haemodynamically favourable relative to
the alternatives and preserves respiratory drive; flagging it would
push a medic away from the safer agent.
map       DERIVED, not captured: (SBP + 2*DBP)/3, rounded, recomputed
whenever either pressure moves and carrying the age of the older
of the two. The band below therefore only ever validates a MAP a
medic STATED — they may be reading an arterial line — and a
stated MAP supersedes the derived one until a newer pressure
arrives. It spans everything derivable from the sbp and dbp bands
above, so a derived value cannot fail a range its inputs passed.
temp      the one vital a medic states in two units, so it carries two
bands: min/max in `unit` (C, the unit the cautions below are
written in) and alt_min/alt_max in `alt_unit` (F). A stated unit
is checked against its own band; an unlabelled number is read as
whichever band it falls in, and the bands do not overlap. A value
in neither is rejected visibly rather than stored in a unit it
was never given in.
The reading keeps the unit it was stated in — a medic who typed
104 F is shown 104 F — and carries both conversions. Only the
canonical Celsius value is compared against the table below.
NOTE: min 35 excludes hypothermia stated in Celsius. 'temp 33' is
rejected, and hypothermia_txa can then only arm from a Fahrenheit
reading (93-94.9F is 33.9-34.9C). Lowering temp.min here restores
it with no code change.
glucose   TWO units whose plausible bands OVERLAP, which temperature's do
not: 32 is a critical low in mg/dL and a high in mmol/L, the
opposite emergency. A stated unit is always honoured. An
UNLABELLED value is read as `assumed_unit_when_unstated`, and
the assumption is written into the reading and quoted back in
the caution, so it is visible rather than silent.
THE DEFAULT IS A CLINICAL CONVENTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and it
is config for that reason. It is set to mg/dL because the whole
corpus is US JTS/TCCC. A deployment where medics state mmol/L
changes this line and nothing else. Flagged for owner
ratification — see the round-1 PR notes.
when.<flag>  a rule may also arm on a boolean fact about the patient
rather than a measurement — `ams_stated` is the first. Written
{"is": true}. These come from PatientContext, not from the
vitals table, because a stated descriptor is not a measurement.

cautions.caution: {drug} carries a hypotension risk and the recorded SBP is {sbp} mmHg. Confirm the haemodynamic plan before giving it.
{drug} carries a hypotension risk and the recorded MAP is {map} mmHg. Confirm the haemodynamic plan before giving it.
{drug} is a respiratory depressant and the recorded RR is {rr}/min. Confirm airway and ventilation support before giving it.
{drug} is a respiratory depressant and the recorded SpO2 is {spo2}%. Confirm oxygenation and airway support before giving it.
{drug} slows AV conduction and the recorded HR is {hr} bpm. Confirm the rhythm before giving it.
The recorded temperature is {temp}. TXA is for traumatic haemorrhagic shock, not hypothermia — confirm active haemorrhage.
The recorded GCS is {gcs}. Anything by mouth carries an aspiration risk at this level of consciousness.
The patient is described as having altered mental status. Anything by mouth carries an aspiration risk until they are protecting their own airway.
The recorded glucose is {glucose}. Treat the hypoglycaemia, and give nothing by mouth unless the patient is fully awake and protecting their airway.
